notes.body:
Check the pipeline result:
Checking commit: 409a6790 Allow further processing of SmbDirect packet with in-band data that spans packets
Warning: keep lines in the commit message under 80 characters.
Please rewrite your commit message to our standards, matching this format:
    component: a very brief summary of the change
    A commit message should start with a brief summary, followed by a single
    blank line and an optional longer description. If the change is specific to
    a single protocol, start the summary line with the abbreviated name of the
    protocol and a colon.
    Use paragraphs to improve readability. Limit each line to 80 characters.

What is the underlying RDMA protocol? Maybe that needs to reassamble things before passing data
to dissect_smb_direct_iwarp_heur or dissect_smb_direct_infiniband[_heur].

If len is smaller than data_length, we have truncated payload...
changed the description

changed title from **Draft: Allow further processing of SmbDirect packet with in-band data that spans packets** to **Draft: {+Smb-Direct: +}Allow further processing of SmbDirect packet with in-band data that spans packets**
changed the description

The underlying RDMA protocol here is ROCeV2/infiniband.  In an example I'm looking at this comes across as an SmbDirect DataMessage and then followed by several "ROCE RC Send Middle" packets and then a "ROCE RC Send Last".  Are you saying you'd like that folded into a single SmbDirect DataMessage in the UI that is made up of all those packets?
Yes, I guess it would be similar to https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/commit/9ec5208873b7ae92373e1288fa318e133acaab43 where I did it for iwrap.

You could also put it into dissect_smb_direct_infiniband(), as it might be easier than
doing it in parse_PAYLOAD()...

We may only need RC_SEND_FIRST, RC_SEND_MIDDLE and RC_SEND_LAST
and I guess RC_SEND_LAST_INVAL is missing...
I guess these are the only ones used for smb-direct

RC_SEND_ONLY and RC_SEND_ONLY_INVAL is what see in captures between a linux client and server,
for non fragmented requests.

What is your setup? And are you seeing in non fragmented requests?

In the single packet case, it works and I see the SmbDirect DataMessage parsed by a higher-level parser correctly. In the fragmented case, I see the SmbDirect DataMessage (which ideally is processed further by a higher-level parser), some number of RC_SEND_MIDDLE followed by an RC_SEND_LAST.  One option here which is I think what you did for iwarp is to have the RRoce Middle and Last messages show the SmbDirect attributes in a similar fashion to TCP fragmentation which will show the seq/ack/win/len values for the TCP reassembly of the TLS packet (as an example).  That may be what you're looking for here or am I missing something?

What is the RC_SEND* type for the working messages?

The fragmented should start with RC_SEND_FIRST,
but the non-fragmented ones are RC_SEND_ONLY?
It is an RC_SEND_FIRST in the multi-fragment case and RC_SEND_ONLY_INVAL in the single packet case.
This might be a replacement for this MR https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18745 ... but it needs testing

Apologies for the delay as I've been away from work.  I will update this pull request to provide a capture extract that exhibits this behavior. Let me know if email is a better forum for this discussion. 
Stefan, with your infiniband parser changes and my suggested change included here, the packet now correctly shows up both at the Smb-Direct layer and at the higher-level protocol parsing.  With just your infiniband changes, the Smb-Direct layer parses it correctly but still doesn't pass the packet on to the higher-level parser.  I can provide screenshots of master/WithYourChange/WithBothChanges to show the differences if that helps.

Thanks for testing, screenshots are better than nothing.

But I don't understand yet, why your change would be needed.

So captures would be the best way forward...

I've added an extract that exhibits the problem.  Have also attached screen shots of the following:

current main branch:
  ![MainBranch](/uploads/7b97524a7e923f333533ecea448fe5f5/MainBranch.JPG)

Stefan's rocev2 fix only:
![MetzBranch](/uploads/87d99d901133e7d95c8e0f5fabd67ef7/MetzBranch.JPG)


Stefan's fix with just higher level protocol:
![MetzBranchWithHigherLevelParser](/uploads/35e5a0b48fab9191034df09e13eb0d58/MetzBranchWithHigherLevelParser.JPG)

Stefan's fix with this SmbDirect Fix:
![MetzBranchWithSmbDirectFix](/uploads/d49f8d624076d84ef8511ea93ed2ecfc/MetzBranchWithSmbDirectFix.JPG)

Finally Stefan's fix with this SmbDirect fix and higher level protocol:
![MetzBranchWithSmbDirectFixAndHigherLevelParser](/uploads/5c9ab4696d3ad8015c08c49782b2a6c2/MetzBranchWithSmbDirectFixAndHigherLevelParser.JPG)

Ok, thanks for the capture.

My patch doesn't work as expected, so only your patch is
effective.

What we need to see is an SMBDirect message on top of re-assambled InfiniBand RC Send messages
in frame 5.

I'm going through this in a debugger now.
I guess find_or_create_conversation() and find_conversation_pinfo()
are not working correctly because of the strange Infiniband UDP interaction,
which clears pinfo->*ports.

Ok, the latest version in !18745 works for me without any other patches.

Please check :-)

Pulled your current changes for ROCE parser and it works fine.  I assume it was your intention to have the top-level parser packet not show until the last segment is processed.  This is very different from past behavior where the packet was parsed starting with first one.  It's fine.  This particular change to SmbDirect is no longer needed.  Do you want me to just checkin the trace extract? It may be valuable to have that in the test capture collection here.  That would be a separate checkin that I could do or you could pull it into one of yours in the future.
Have reduced this pull request just to an SmbDirect multi-packet sample capture
